Place them in:\n\n- Global: `~/.config/opencode/agents/`\n- Per-project: `.opencode/agents/`\n\n```\n---\n\ndescription: Reviews code for quality and best practices\n\nmode: subagent\n\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514\n\ntemperature: 0.1\n\npermission:\n\n  edit: deny\n\n  bash: deny\n\n---\n\nYou are in code review mode. Focus on:\n\n- Code quality and best practices\n\n- Potential bugs and edge cases\n\n- Performance implications\n\n- Security considerations\n\nProvide constructive feedback without making direct changes.\n```\n\nThe markdown file name becomes the agent name. For example, `review.md` creates a `review` agent.\n\n* * *\n\n## [Options](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#options)\n\nLet’s look at these configuration options in detail.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Description](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#description)\n\nUse the `description` option to provide a brief description of what the agent does and when to use it.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"review\": {\n\n      \"description\": \"Reviews code for best practices and potential issues\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThis is a **required** config option.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Temperature](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#temperature)\n\nControl the randomness and creativity of the LLM’s responses with the `temperature` config.\n\nLower values make responses more focused and deterministic, while higher values increase creativity and variability.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"plan\": {\n\n      \"temperature\": 0.1\n\n    },\n\n    \"creative\": {\n\n      \"temperature\": 0.8\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nTemperature values typically range from 0.0 to 1.0:\n\n- **0.0-0.2**: Very focused and deterministic responses, ideal for code analysis and planning\n- **0.3-0.5**: Balanced responses with some creativity, good for general development tasks\n- **0.6-1.0**: More creative and varied responses, useful for brainstorming and exploration\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"analyze\": {\n\n      \"temperature\": 0.1,\n\n      \"prompt\": \"{file:./prompts/analysis.txt}\"\n\n    },\n\n    \"build\": {\n\n      \"temperature\": 0.3\n\n    },\n\n    \"brainstorm\": {\n\n      \"temperature\": 0.7,\n\n      \"prompt\": \"{file:./prompts/creative.txt}\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nIf no temperature is specified, OpenCode uses model-specific defaults; typically 0 for most models, 0.55 for Qwen models.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Max steps](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#max-steps)\n\nControl the maximum number of agentic iterations an agent can perform before being forced to respond with text only. This allows users who wish to control costs to set a limit on agentic actions.\n\nIf this is not set, the agent will continue to iterate until the model chooses to stop or the user interrupts the session.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"quick-thinker\": {\n\n      \"description\": \"Fast reasoning with limited iterations\",\n\n      \"prompt\": \"You are a quick thinker. Solve problems with minimal steps.\",\n\n      \"steps\": 5\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nWhen the limit is reached, the agent receives a special system prompt instructing it to respond with a summarization of its work and recommended remaining tasks.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Disable](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#disable)\n\nSet to `true` to disable the agent.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"review\": {\n\n      \"disable\": true\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\n* * *\n\n### [Prompt](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#prompt)\n\nSpecify a custom system prompt file for this agent with the `prompt` config. The prompt file should contain instructions specific to the agent’s purpose.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"review\": {\n\n      \"prompt\": \"{file:./prompts/code-review.txt}\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThis path is relative to where the config file is located. So this works for both the global OpenCode config and the project specific config.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Model](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#model)\n\nUse the `model` config to override the model for this agent. Useful for using different models optimized for different tasks. For example, a faster model for planning, a more capable model for implementation.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"plan\": {\n\n      \"model\": \"anthropic/claude-haiku-4-20250514\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThe model ID in your OpenCode config uses the format `provider/model-id`. For example, if you’re using [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen), you would use `opencode/gpt-5.1-codex` for GPT 5.1 Codex.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Tools (deprecated)](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#tools-deprecated)\n\n`tools` is **deprecated**. Prefer the agent’s [`permission`](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/#permissions) field for new configs, updates and more fine-grained control.\n\nAllows you to control which tools are available in this agent. You can enable or disable specific tools by setting them to `true` or `false`. In an agent’s `tools` config, `true` is equivalent to `{\"*\": \"allow\"}` permission and `false` is equivalent to `{\"*\": \"deny\"}` permission.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"tools\": {\n\n    \"write\": true,\n\n    \"bash\": true\n\n  },\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"plan\": {\n\n      \"tools\": {\n\n        \"write\": false,\n\n        \"bash\": false\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nYou can also use wildcards in legacy `tools` entries to control multiple tools at once. For example, to disable all tools from an MCP server:\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"readonly\": {\n\n      \"tools\": {\n\n        \"mymcp_*\": false,\n\n        \"write\": false,\n\n        \"edit\": false\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\n[Learn more about tools](https://opencode.ai/docs/tools).\n\n* * *\n\n### [Permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#permissions)\n\nYou can configure permissions to manage what actions an agent can take. Each permission key can be set to:\n\n- `\"ask\"` — Prompt for approval before running the tool\n- `\"allow\"` — Allow all operations without approval\n- `\"deny\"` — Disable the tool\n\nThe available permission keys are:\n\n| Key | Tools it gates |\n| --- | --- |\n| `read` | `read` |\n| `edit` | `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch` |\n| `glob` | `glob` |\n| `grep` | `grep` |\n| `list` | `list` |\n| `bash` | `bash` |\n| `task` | `task` |\n| `external_directory` | Any tool that reads or writes files outside the project worktree |\n| `webfetch` | `webfetch` |\n| `websearch` | `websearch` |\n| `lsp` | `lsp` |\n| `skill` | `skill` |\n| `question` | `question` |\n| `doom_loop` | Recovery prompts when an agent appears stuck |\n\n`read`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `list`, `bash`, `task`, `external_directory`, `lsp`, and `skill` accept either a shorthand action (`\"allow\" | \"ask\" | \"deny\"`) or an object of glob/pattern → action for fine-grained control. The remaining keys accept the shorthand action only.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"permission\": {\n\n    \"edit\": \"deny\"\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nYou can override these permissions per agent.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"permission\": {\n\n    \"edit\": \"deny\"\n\n  },\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"build\": {\n\n      \"permission\": {\n\n        \"edit\": \"ask\"\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nYou can also set permissions in Markdown agents.\n\n```\n---\n\ndescription: Code review without edits\n\nmode: subagent\n\npermission:\n\n  edit: deny\n\n  bash:\n\n    \"*\": ask\n\n    \"git diff\": allow\n\n    \"git log*\": allow\n\n    \"grep *\": allow\n\n  webfetch: deny\n\n---\n\nOnly analyze code and suggest changes.\n```\n\nYou can set permissions for specific bash commands.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"build\": {\n\n      \"permission\": {\n\n        \"bash\": {\n\n          \"git push\": \"ask\",\n\n          \"grep *\": \"allow\"\n\n        }\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThis can take a glob pattern.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"build\": {\n\n      \"permission\": {\n\n        \"bash\": {\n\n          \"git *\": \"ask\"\n\n        }\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nAnd you can also use the `*` wildcard to manage permissions for all commands.\nSince the last matching rule takes precedence, put the `*` wildcard first and specific rules after.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"build\": {\n\n      \"permission\": {\n\n        \"bash\": {\n\n          \"*\": \"ask\",\n\n          \"git status *\": \"allow\"\n\n        }\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\n[Learn more about permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions).\n\n* * *\n\n### [Mode](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#mode)\n\nControl the agent’s mode with the `mode` config. The `mode` option is used to determine how the agent can be used.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"review\": {\n\n      \"mode\": \"subagent\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThe `mode` option can be set to `primary`, `subagent`, or `all`. If no `mode` is specified, it defaults to `all`.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Hidden](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#hidden)\n\nHide a subagent from the `@` autocomplete menu with `hidden: true`. Useful for internal subagents that should only be invoked programmatically by other agents via the Task tool.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"internal-helper\": {\n\n      \"mode\": \"subagent\",\n\n      \"hidden\": true\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThis only affects user visibility in the autocomplete menu. Hidden agents can still be invoked by the model via the Task tool if permissions allow.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Task permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#task-permissions)\n\nControl which subagents an agent can invoke via the Task tool with `permission.task`. Uses glob patterns for flexible matching.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"orchestrator\": {\n\n      \"mode\": \"primary\",\n\n      \"permission\": {\n\n        \"task\": {\n\n          \"*\": \"deny\",\n\n          \"orchestrator-*\": \"allow\",\n\n          \"code-reviewer\": \"ask\"\n\n        }\n\n      }\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nWhen set to `deny`, the subagent is removed from the Task tool description entirely, so the model won’t attempt to invoke it.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Color](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#color)\n\nCustomize the agent’s visual appearance in the UI with the `color` option. This affects how the agent appears in the interface.\n\nUse a valid hex color (e.g., `#FF5733`) or theme color: `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"creative\": {\n\n      \"color\": \"#ff6b6b\"\n\n    },\n\n    \"code-reviewer\": {\n\n      \"color\": \"accent\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\n* * *\n\n### [Top P](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#top-p)\n\nControl response diversity with the `top_p` option. Alternative to temperature for controlling randomness.\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"brainstorm\": {\n\n      \"top_p\": 0.9\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nValues range from 0.0 to 1.0. Lower values are more focused, higher values more diverse.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Additional](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#additional)\n\nAny other options you specify in your agent configuration will be **passed through directly** to the provider as model options. This allows you to use provider-specific features and parameters.\n\nFor example, with OpenAI’s reasoning models, you can control the reasoning effort:\n\n```\n{\n\n  \"agent\": {\n\n    \"deep-thinker\": {\n\n      \"description\": \"Agent that uses high reasoning effort for complex problems\",\n\n      \"model\": \"openai/gpt-5\",\n\n      \"reasoningEffort\": \"high\",\n\n      \"textVerbosity\": \"low\"\n\n    }\n\n  }\n\n}\n```\n\nThese additional options are model and provider-specific. Check your provider’s documentation for available parameters.\n\n* * *\n\n## [Create agents](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#create-agents)\n\nYou can create new agents using the following command:\n\n```\nopencode agent create\n```\n\nThis interactive command will:\n\n1. Ask where to save the agent; global or project-specific.\n2. Description of what the agent should do.\n3. Generate an appropriate system prompt and identifier.\n4. Let you select which permissions the agent should be allowed (anything you don’t select is denied).\n5. Finally, create a markdown file with the agent configuration.\n\n* * *\n\n## [Use cases](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#use-cases)\n\nHere are some common use cases for different agents.\n\n- **Build agent**: Full development work with all tools enabled\n- **Plan agent**: Analysis and planning without making changes\n- **Review agent**: Code review with read-only access plus documentation tools\n- **Debug agent**: Focused on investigation with bash and read tools enabled\n- **Docs agent**: Documentation writing with file operations but no system commands\n\n* * *\n\n## [Examples](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#examples)\n\nHere are some example agents you might find useful.\n\n* * *\n\n### [Documentation agent](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#documentation-agent)\n\n```\n---\n\ndescription: Writes and maintains project documentation\n\nmode: subagent\n\npermission:\n\n  bash: deny\n\n---\n\nYou are a technical writer. Create clear, comprehensive documentation.\n\nFocus on:\n\n- Clear explanations\n\n- Proper structure\n\n- Code examples\n\n- User-friendly language\n```\n\n* * *\n\n### [Security auditor](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/\\#security-auditor)\n\n```\n---\n\ndescription: Performs security audits and identifies vulnerabilities\n\nmode: subagent\n\npermission:\n\n  edit: deny\n\n---\n\nYou are a security expert. Focus on identifying potential security issues.\n\nLook for:\n\n- Input validation vulnerabilities\n\n- Authentication and authorization flaws\n\n- Data exposure risks\n\n- Dependency vulnerabilities\n\n- Configuration security issues\n```","metadata":{"og:type":"article","ogUrl":"https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/","title":"Agents | OpenCode","language":"en","ogImage":"https://social-cards.sst.dev/opencode-docs/QWdlbnRz.png?desc=Configure%20and%20use%20specialized%20agents.","og:locale":"en","og:description":"Configure and use specialized agents.","generator":["Astro v5.7.13","Starlight v0.34.3"],"ogSiteName":"OpenCode","og:site_name":"OpenCode","og:url":"https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/","description":"Configure and use specialized agents.","ogLocale":"en","ogTitle":"Agents","twitter:image":"https://social-cards.sst.dev/opencode-docs/QWdlbnRz.png?desc=Configure%20and%20use%20specialized%20agents.","og:image":"https://social-cards.sst.dev/opencode-docs/QWdlbnRz.png?desc=Configure%20and%20use%20specialized%20agents.","viewport":"width=device-width, initial-scale=1","twitter:card":"summary_large_image","og:title":"Agents","ogDescription":"Configure and use specialized agents.","favicon":"https://opencode.ai/favicon-v3.ico","scrapeId":"01a1295b-240d-7369-a7c2-0e01bd02bfcf","sourceURL":"https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/","url":"https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/","statusCode":200,"contentType":"text/html","proxyUsed":"basic","cacheState":"hit","cachedAt":"2026-10-11T03:43:06.311Z","creditsUsed":1,"concurrencyLimited":false}},"isError":false}

Yes—your flow is right. Don’t paste the Proton link or API key into chat again; that shared link is sensitive. Open it yourself, copy the OpenRouter key locally, then revoke/rotate the share/key afterward if it was exposed beyond your team.

1. In OpenRouter, add the $20 credit and create a dedicated API key with a $20 spending limit.

2. In PowerShell, open the project and start OpenCode:

```powershell
cd D:\Personal_Projects\TUM_HackathonFinal
opencode
```

3. Inside OpenCode, run:

```text
/connect
```

Choose **OpenRouter** → **API key** → paste the key directly into the prompt.

4. Select the requested model:

```text
/models
```

Search for and select:

```text
openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor
```

If it does not appear, restart OpenCode. If it still is missing, add this to the project’s `opencode.json`—merge it with any existing configuration; do not overwrite it:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "model": "openrouter/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor",
  "provider": {
    "openrouter": {
      "models": {
        "meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor": {}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

OpenRouter’s current instructions confirm `/connect` → OpenRouter → API key, then `/models`; the model slug above is correct. [OpenRouter’s OpenCode guide](https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/coding-agents/opencode-integration) · [model page](https://openrouter.ai/meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor)

For the “fleet,” start with one coordinating Build agent and use read-only subagents first:

```text
Read AGENTS.md and .entire/agent-guide.md. Use Entire before investigating.
Delegate code discovery to @explore and external research to @scout.
Do not make concurrent edits in the shared working tree.
Keep commits atomic, never use --no-verify, and push checkpoints after each meaningful change.
```

Then ask the main agent to use `@general` only for one clearly owned write task at a time. That avoids agents overwriting each other. The project’s submitted RFQ agent must still remain within its four-browser maximum; OpenCode subagents do not justify launching extra challenge browsers.

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

# Intro

Get started with OpenCode.

[**OpenCode**](https://opencode.ai/) is an open source AI coding agent. It’s available as a terminal-based interface, desktop app, or IDE extension.

![OpenCode TUI with the opencode theme](https://opencode.ai/docs/_astro/screenshot.CQjBbRyJ_1dLadc.webp)

Let’s get started.

* * *

#### [Prerequisites](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#prerequisites)

To use OpenCode in your terminal, you’ll need:

1. A modern terminal emulator like:
   - [WezTerm](https://wezterm.org/), cross-platform
   - [Alacritty](https://alacritty.org/), cross-platform
   - [Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/), Linux and macOS
   - [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/), Linux and macOS
2. API keys for the LLM providers you want to use.


* * *

## [Install](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#install)

The easiest way to install OpenCode 1 is through the install script. These installation methods provide the `opencode`
binary and can conflict with or replace an OpenCode 2 installation.

```
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
```

You can also install it with the following commands:

- **Using Node.js**




  - [npm](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-0)
  - [Bun](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-1)
  - [pnpm](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-2)
  - [Yarn](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-3)

```
npm install -g opencode-ai
```

```
bun install -g opencode-ai
```

```
pnpm install -g opencode-ai
```

```
yarn global add opencode-ai
```

- **Using Homebrew on macOS and Linux**



```
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode
```














> We recommend using the OpenCode tap for the most up to date releases. The official `brew install opencode` formula is maintained by the Homebrew team and is updated less frequently.

- **Installing on Arch Linux**



```
sudo pacman -S opencode           # Arch Linux (Stable)

paru -S opencode-bin              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
```


#### [Windows](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#windows)

- **Using Chocolatey**



```
choco install opencode
```

- **Using Scoop**



```
scoop install opencode
```

- **Using NPM**



```
npm install -g opencode-ai
```

- **Using Mise**



```
mise use -g github:anomalyco/opencode
```

- **Using Docker**



```
docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode
```


Support for installing OpenCode on Windows using Bun is currently in progress.

You can also grab the binary from the [Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases).

* * *

## [Configure](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#configure)

With OpenCode you can use any LLM provider by configuring their API keys.

If you are new to using LLM providers, we recommend using [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen).
It’s a curated list of models that have been tested and verified by the OpenCode
team.

1. Run the `/connect` command in the TUI, select opencode, and head to [opencode.ai/auth](https://opencode.ai/auth).



```
/connect
```

2. Sign in, add your billing details, and copy your API key.

3. Paste your API key.



```
┌ API key

│

│

└ enter
```


Alternatively, you can select one of the other providers. [Learn more](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers#directory).

* * *

## [Initialize](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#initialize)

Now that you’ve configured a provider, you can navigate to a project that
you want to work on.

```
cd /path/to/project
```

And run OpenCode.

```
opencode
```

Next, initialize OpenCode for the project by running the following command.

```
/init
```

This will get OpenCode to analyze your project and create an `AGENTS.md` file in
the project root.

This helps OpenCode understand the project structure and the coding patterns
used.

* * *

## [Usage](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#usage)

You are now ready to use OpenCode to work on your project. Feel free to ask it
anything!

If you are new to using an AI coding agent, here are some examples that might
help.

* * *

### [Ask questions](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#ask-questions)

You can ask OpenCode to explain the codebase to you.

```
How is authentication handled in @packages/functions/src/api/index.ts
```

This is helpful if there’s a part of the codebase that you didn’t work on.

* * *

### [Add features](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#add-features)

You can ask OpenCode to add new features to your project. Though we first recommend asking it to create a plan.

1. **Create a plan**

OpenCode has a _Plan mode_ that disables its ability to make changes and
instead suggest _how_ it’ll implement the feature.

Switch to it using the **Tab** key. You’ll see an indicator for this in the lower right corner.



```
<TAB>
```













Now let’s describe what we want it to do.



```
When a user deletes a note, we'd like to flag it as deleted in the database.

Then create a screen that shows all the recently deleted notes.

From this screen, the user can undelete a note or permanently delete it.
```













You want to give OpenCode enough details to understand what you want. It helps
to talk to it like you are talking to a junior developer on your team.

2. **Iterate on the plan**

Once it gives you a plan, you can give it feedback or add more details.



```
We'd like to design this new screen using a design I've used before.

[Image #1] Take a look at this image and use it as a reference.
```













OpenCode can scan any images you give it and add them to the prompt. You can
do this by dragging and dropping an image into the terminal.

3. **Build the feature**

Once you feel comfortable with the plan, switch back to _Build mode_ by
hitting the **Tab** key again.



```
<TAB>
```













And asking it to make the changes.



```
Sounds good! Go ahead and make the changes.
```


* * *

### [Make changes](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#make-changes)

For more straightforward changes, you can ask OpenCode to directly build it
without having to review the plan first.

```
We need to add authentication to the /settings route. Take a look at how this is

handled in the /notes route in @packages/functions/src/notes.ts and implement

the same logic in @packages/functions/src/settings.ts
```

You want to make sure you provide a good amount of detail so OpenCode makes the right
changes.

* * *

### [Undo changes](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#undo-changes)

Let’s say you ask OpenCode to make some changes.

```
Can you refactor the function in @packages/functions/src/api/index.ts?
```

But you realize that it is not what you wanted. You **can undo** the changes
using the `/undo` command.

```
/undo
```

OpenCode will now revert the changes you made and show your original message
again.

```
Can you refactor the function in @packages/functions/src/api/index.ts?
```

From here you can tweak the prompt and ask OpenCode to try again.

Or you **can redo** the changes using the `/redo` command.

```
/redo
```

* * *

The conversations that you have with OpenCode can be [shared with your\\
team](https://opencode.ai/docs/share).

```
/share
```

This will create a link to the current conversation and copy it to your clipboard.

Here’s an [example conversation](https://opencode.ai/s/4XP1fce5) with OpenCode.

* * *

## [Customize](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#customize)

And that’s it! You are now a pro at using OpenCode.

To make it your own, we recommend [picking a theme](https://opencode.ai/docs/themes), [customizing the keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds), [configuring code formatters](https://opencode.ai/docs/formatters), [creating custom commands](https://opencode.ai/docs/commands), or playing around with the [OpenCode config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config).",

[NewOpenCode v2 is now available→](https://opencode.ai/v2)

# Intro

Get started with OpenCode.

[**OpenCode**](https://opencode.ai/) is an open source AI coding agent. It’s available as a terminal-based interface, desktop app, or IDE extension.

![OpenCode TUI with the opencode theme](https://opencode.ai/docs/_astro/screenshot.CQjBbRyJ_1dLadc.webp)

Let’s get started.

* * *

#### [Prerequisites](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#prerequisites)

To use OpenCode in your terminal, you’ll need:

1. A modern terminal emulator like:
   - [WezTerm](https://wezterm.org/), cross-platform
   - [Alacritty](https://alacritty.org/), cross-platform
   - [Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/), Linux and macOS
   - [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/), Linux and macOS
2. API keys for the LLM providers you want to use.


* * *

## [Install](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#install)

The easiest way to install OpenCode 1 is through the install script. These installation methods provide the `opencode`
binary and can conflict with or replace an OpenCode 2 installation.

```
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
```

You can also install it with the following commands:

- **Using Node.js**




  - [npm](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-0)
  - [Bun](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-1)
  - [pnpm](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-2)
  - [Yarn](https://opencode.ai/docs/#tab-panel-3)

```
npm install -g opencode-ai
```

```
bun install -g opencode-ai
```

```
pnpm install -g opencode-ai
```

```
yarn global add opencode-ai
```

- **Using Homebrew on macOS and Linux**



```
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode
```














> We recommend using the OpenCode tap for the most up to date releases. The official `brew install opencode` formula is maintained by the Homebrew team and is updated less frequently.

- **Installing on Arch Linux**



```
sudo pacman -S opencode           # Arch Linux (Stable)

paru -S opencode-bin              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
```


#### [Windows](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#windows)

- **Using Chocolatey**



```
choco install opencode
```

- **Using Scoop**



```
scoop install opencode
```

- **Using NPM**



```
npm install -g opencode-ai
```

- **Using Mise**



```
mise use -g github:anomalyco/opencode
```

- **Using Docker**



```
docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode
```


Support for installing OpenCode on Windows using Bun is currently in progress.

You can also grab the binary from the [Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases).

* * *

## [Configure](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#configure)

With OpenCode you can use any LLM provider by configuring their API keys.

If you are new to using LLM providers, we recommend using [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen).
It’s a curated list of models that have been tested and verified by the OpenCode
team.

1. Run the `/connect` command in the TUI, select opencode, and head to [opencode.ai/auth](https://opencode.ai/auth).



```
/connect
```

2. Sign in, add your billing details, and copy your API key.

3. Paste your API key.



```
┌ API key

│

│

└ enter
```


Alternatively, you can select one of the other providers. [Learn more](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers#directory).

* * *

## [Initialize](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#initialize)

Now that you’ve configured a provider, you can navigate to a project that
you want to work on.

```
cd /path/to/project
```

And run OpenCode.

```
opencode
```

Next, initialize OpenCode for the project by running the following command.

```
/init
```

This will get OpenCode to analyze your project and create an `AGENTS.md` file in
the project root.

This helps OpenCode understand the project structure and the coding patterns
used.

* * *

## [Usage](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#usage)

You are now ready to use OpenCode to work on your project. Feel free to ask it
anything!

If you are new to using an AI coding agent, here are some examples that might
help.

* * *

### [Ask questions](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#ask-questions)

You can ask OpenCode to explain the codebase to you.

```
How is authentication handled in @packages/functions/src/api/index.ts
```

This is helpful if there’s a part of the codebase that you didn’t work on.

* * *

### [Add features](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#add-features)

You can ask OpenCode to add new features to your project. Though we first recommend asking it to create a plan.

1. **Create a plan**

OpenCode has a _Plan mode_ that disables its ability to make changes and
instead suggest _how_ it’ll implement the feature.

Switch to it using the **Tab** key. You’ll see an indicator for this in the lower right corner.



```
<TAB>
```













Now let’s describe what we want it to do.



```
When a user deletes a note, we'd like to flag it as deleted in the database.

Then create a screen that shows all the recently deleted notes.

From this screen, the user can undelete a note or permanently delete it.
```













You want to give OpenCode enough details to understand what you want. It helps
to talk to it like you are talking to a junior developer on your team.

2. **Iterate on the plan**

Once it gives you a plan, you can give it feedback or add more details.



```
We'd like to design this new screen using a design I've used before.

[Image #1] Take a look at this image and use it as a reference.
```













OpenCode can scan any images you give it and add them to the prompt. You can
do this by dragging and dropping an image into the terminal.

3. **Build the feature**

Once you feel comfortable with the plan, switch back to _Build mode_ by
hitting the **Tab** key again.



```
<TAB>
```













And asking it to make the changes.



```
Sounds good! Go ahead and make the changes.
```


* * *

### [Make changes](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#make-changes)

For more straightforward changes, you can ask OpenCode to directly build it
without having to review the plan first.

```
We need to add authentication to the /settings route. Take a look at how this is

handled in the /notes route in @packages/functions/src/notes.ts and implement

the same logic in @packages/functions/src/settings.ts
```

You want to make sure you provide a good amount of detail so OpenCode makes the right
changes.

* * *

### [Undo changes](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#undo-changes)

Let’s say you ask OpenCode to make some changes.

```
Can you refactor the function in @packages/functions/src/api/index.ts?
```

But you realize that it is not what you wanted. You **can undo** the changes
using the `/undo` command.

```
/undo
```

OpenCode will now revert the changes you made and show your original message
again.

```
Can you refactor the function in @packages/functions/src/api/index.ts?
```

From here you can tweak the prompt and ask OpenCode to try again.

Or you **can redo** the changes using the `/redo` command.

```
/redo
```

* * *

The conversations that you have with OpenCode can be [shared with your\\
team](https://opencode.ai/docs/share).

```
/share
```

This will create a link to the current conversation and copy it to your clipboard.

Here’s an [example conversation](https://opencode.ai/s/4XP1fce5) with OpenCode.

* * *

## [Customize](https://opencode.ai/docs/\#customize)

And that’s it! You are now a pro at using OpenCode.

To make it your own, we recommend [picking a theme](https://opencode.ai/docs/themes), [customizing the keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds), [configuring code formatters](https://opencode.ai/docs/formatters), [creating custom commands](https://opencode.ai/docs/commands), or playing around with the [OpenCode config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config).","metadata":{"language":"en","generator":["Astro v5.7.13","Starlight v0.34.3"],"ogLocale":"en","og:title":"Intro","description":"Get started with OpenCode.","ogDescription":"Get started with OpenCode.","og:type":"article","title":"Intro | AI coding agent built for the terminal","og:site_name":"OpenCode","og:url":"https://opencode.ai/docs/","twitter:card":"summary_large_image","ogUrl":"https://opencode.ai/docs/","og:image":"https://social-cards.sst.dev/opencode-docs/SW50cm8%3D.png?desc=Get%20started%20with%20OpenCode.","ogTitle":"Intro","twitter:image":"https://social-cards.sst.dev/opencode-docs/SW50cm8%3D.png?desc=Get%20started%20with%20OpenCode.","viewport":"width=device-width, initial-scale=1","og:description":"Get started with OpenCode.","ogImage":"https://social-cards.sst.dev/opencode-docs/SW50cm8%3D.png?desc=Get%20started%20with%20OpenCode.","ogSiteName":"OpenCode","og:locale":"en","favicon":"https://opencode.ai/favicon-v3.ico","scrapeId":"01a1295d-ccf2-70ae-9374-b9f8bc6740b2","sourceURL":"https://opencode.ai/docs/","url":"https://opencode.ai/docs/","statusCode":200,"contentType":"text/html","proxyUsed":"basic","cacheState":"hit","cachedAt":"2026-10-11T03:14:08.577Z","creditsUsed":1,"concurrencyLimited":false}},"isError":false}

web.title: Changing a Model
web.description:
#### Openrouter provider routing, reasoning and output cap

For `openrouter/...` models you can optionally restrict which upstream providers Openrouter uses, control reasoning, and cap the completion length. All keys live in the `[openrouter]` section of `configuration.toml`. Reasoning-capable models are those litellm's bundled reasoning metadata flags over the model id and its provider-prefixed/`xai/`-forms, the maintained Grok registry, or `config.additional_reasoning_effort_models`; they inherit `config.reasoning_effort` unless an Openrouter-specific effort or token budget is set.

```toml
[openrouter]
# Uncomment and adjust the keys you need; unset keys keep Openrouter's defaults.
# provider_only = ["z-ai"]             # hard allowlist of upstream providers; empty = default routing
# provider_order = ["z-ai", "novita"]  # preferred order instead of an allowlist; ignored when provider_only is set
# allow_fallbacks = true               # when provider_order is set, allow routing beyond the list
# reasoning_effort = "low"             # override global effort: "none", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh" or "max"
# reasoning_max_tokens = 2048          # explicit budget; ignored only when final effort remains "none"
# max_tokens = 16000                   # hard cap on completion tokens for the request
```

`provider_only` and `reasoning_effort = "none"` are useful to pin a specific provider and to bound the cost of reasoning models. Because Openrouter treats effort and token budgets as mutually exclusive, an explicit Openrouter-specific `"none"` keeps reasoning disabled when the model supports disabling it. Grok 4.5/4.6, Gemini 3.7/3.8 Flash, and the GPT-6 models whose pages omit `"none"` (GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol) clamp it to `"low"` before precedence is applied, so a positive budget wins for those models; explicit Openrouter `"minimal"` remains unchanged for Gemini. Otherwise a positive `reasoning_max_tokens` value takes precedence over the global effort and other Openrouter-specific values. Invalid Openrouter-specific effort values are warned about and treated as unset, so registered reasoning models fall back to `config.reasoning_effort`. Openrouter normalizes `"max"` to `"xhigh"` in this path for LiteLLM/OpenRouter compatibility. Supported effort values vary by model. For models not covered by these clamps, do not assume `"none"` disables reasoning; check the selected model and provider's support. For Anthropic models using a reasoning budget, set the effective output `max_tokens` higher than `reasoning_max_tokens` so the final answer has output headroom. See the Openrouter provider routing and reasoning tokens docs.

### Bug Description

For any model that is **not** covered by `HEURISTIC_MODEL_FAMILY_REGISTRY` and has no entry in `MODEL_ID_OVERRIDES` / `getProviderOverride` (i.e. any self-hosted, private, or otherwise unrecognized `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` model — a local llama.cpp-style server, a custom inference runtime, an internal gateway, etc.), `output.options.reasoningEffort` is **unconditionally deleted** by the `chat.params` hook, even when the model correctly declares a matching `variants` block in `opencode.json` and the user explicitly requests one of those variants via `--variant` / agent `reasoningEffort`.

This reproduces on the current `beta` (`5.0.1`) and is not specific to one model family — it is a structural asymmetry in `getModelCapabilities()`:

```
// packages/model-core/src/model-capabilities/get-model-capabilities.ts
variants: runtimeVariants ?? providerOverride?.variants ?? override?.variants ?? heuristicFamily?.variants,
reasoningEfforts: providerOverride?.reasoningEfforts ?? override?.reasoningEfforts ?? heuristicFamily?.reasoningEfforts,
```

`variants` has a live-config reader (`runtimeVariants`, via `readRuntimeModelVariants(runtimeModel)`), which picks up the model's own `variants: {...}` object from the resolved opencode provider config. `reasoningEfforts` has **no equivalent runtime reader** — it can only ever come from a hardcoded override (`MODEL_ID_OVERRIDES = {}`, empty by default), a hardcoded provider override (`getProviderOverride`, gated to `providerID === "github-copilot"` only), or a name-based heuristic family match.

Because of this, `resolveField()` (`packages/model-core/src/model-settings-compatibility.ts`) always falls through to its last branch for an unrecognized model:

```
if (familyKnown) return { value: undefined, reason: "unsupported-by-model-family" };
return { value: undefined, reason: "unknown-model-family" };
```

Back in `createChatParamsHandler` (`packages/omo-opencode/src/plugin/chat-params.ts`), `compatibility.reasoningEffort === undefined` triggers:

You are responsible for iteratively improving and testing our Atira “RFQ to Bid” agent. Your goal is to achieve a **100/100 quality score while remaining eligible**. Treat eligibility as a hard requirement: a high score without a valid submitted answer does not meet the goal.

1. Read the repository’s `AGENTS.md`, `.entire/agent-guide.md`, and the Atira challenge rules and answer schema.
2. Review the current implementation, existing test results, run logs, and relevant project history. Follow the repository’s Entire workflow where required.

## Testing and improvement loop

Run **one test run at a time**. Do not start another until the current run has completed and been analyzed.

For each iteration:

2. Make a focused change that addresses it.
3. Run the test on the public scenario; do not make a scored submission.

- Keep the system genuinely agentic: the model must make runtime navigation, search, and document-selection decisions.

- Respect the four-browser limit and all challenge rules.
- Generalize to the private dataset and unseen portal layouts; do not overfit to the public scenario.

If repeated runs do not reach 100, continue investigating and report the best verified score, remaining gaps, and the next evidence-based experiment. Do not claim that 100/100 is guaranteed.

# QuoteCraft — from RFQ to bid

A team of model-directed agents that reads a tender across four business websites it has never seen, works out the
bid the rules call for, and enters and signs it in the tender portal.

## How it works

```
task brief ──► model reads it: tender, scenario date, authorized senders
                    │
   ┌────────────────┼──────────────────┬─────────────────┐
   ▼                ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 agent            agent              agent             agent        one per website, each in its own browser:
 tender portal    supplier portal    ERP               webmail      the model picks every click, search and page
   │  keep          │  keep            │  keep           │  keep
   └────────────────┴───────┬──────────┴─────────────────┘
                            ▼
                     shared case file        a model call turns each filed page into typed facts;
                            │                the brief's rules yield the open questions all agents see
                            ▼
                      calculator.py          the bid rules as exact Decimal arithmetic
                            ▼
                     submission agent        fills the bid form it finds; the mail agent fetches the TAN
```

1. **Read the brief.** One model call extracts the tender reference, the scenario date, the bidder and which
   mailbox the rules authorize for which kind of record.
2. **Investigate in parallel.** One agent per website (`worker.Agent`). Each turn it sees its page as accessible
   text with numbered controls (`browser_env.Tab`), plus the case file and its open questions, and answers with
   actions: log in, click, fill, select, search, page through a list, download a file, or `keep` the page as
   evidence. After every browser action, a stable accessible-page fingerprint reports whether the page visibly
   changed, so silent portal failures become recovery hints rather than assumed success. Nothing in the code knows
   a URL, a selector or a click path of any website.
3. **File facts.** `keep` hands the page to a second model call that extracts typed records (positions, Q&A
   answers, revisions, requirements, materials, price conditions, mail records). `casefile.CaseFile` merges them
   and derives what is still unknown. A schema gate rejects malformed extraction envelopes and records before the
   merge. Each successful extraction retains its source URL, site agent, document ID,
   normalized result, and merge summary in the case-file dump, so later agents can assess contradictory evidence.
   A catalogue group found in the specification becomes an ERP question, a key
   in a Q&A answer becomes a mailbox question, and so on. Agents finish when their website has nothing left to add.
4. **Calculate.** `calculator.calculate_bid` applies the bid rules of the brief: latest clarification, withdrawn
   answers, scoped amendments, usable travel, sets to pieces, price scales, FX, conditional discount, condition
   clauses, shared stock, delivery commitments, cartons, pooled setup, project bonus, rounding. A position that
   lacks evidence is left out rather than guessed.
5. **Submit.** `submit.submit_bid` gives the bid to an agent on the tender portal, which fills whatever bid form
   it finds, asks a mail agent for the signing TAN, and runs a fresh live-page pre-submit report immediately before
   the irreversible confirmation. Explicit portal errors and empty required controls block that confirmation.

## What is model and what is code

| The model decides | Code does |
| --- | --- |
| where to go, what to search for, which record or document matters | renders the page, carries out the chosen action |
| how to pass a popup, access check, login or error page | retries a server error, re-reads the page |
| which page is evidence and of what kind | pages through a list the model chose, reads a file it chose |
| what a page says (extraction into typed facts) | parses numbers and dates, checks sender, reference and date |
| when a search is complete or a record does not exist | arithmetic, rounding, allocation |
| how to fill and sign the bid form | — |

No scenario value (reference, material, price, key, login, TAN) appears anywhere in the package.

## Files

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point: reads the run, starts the site agents, calculates, hands the bid to the submission agent |
| `worker.py` | The agent loop: page text in, the model's actions out |
| `browser_env.py` | A tab as accessible text (labels, descriptions, tooltips, frames, collapsed sections) and the actions on it |
| `casefile.py` | Evidence to typed facts with source provenance, open questions, calculator inputs |
| `calculator.py` | The bid rules as Decimal arithmetic |
| `submit.py` | Bid entry and signing |
| `preflight.py` | Non-model live review-page report that gates final confirmation on explicit errors or required inputs |
| `llm.py` | The hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy: JSON replies, retries, a concurrency cap |
| `run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py` | The starter kit's plumbing: the run contract, the run's browsers, the hosted models |
| `agent.json` | Setup (`uv sync`), run command, four browsers, the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The calculator rule by rule, the page rendering against local fixtures, the plumbing against fakes |

## Running it

In the sandbox the platform sets everything (`CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`, `CDP_URLS`, `QWEN_*`):

```sh
atira test-run . --challenge rfq
```

On your machine, against the public websites with the scouting logins (nothing counts), with `atira models proxy`
running in another terminal:

```sh
python ../tools/local_run.py --no-submit
```

Switches: `AGENT_SKIP_SUBMIT=1` stops before the bid form, `AGENT_SITES=a,b` starts only those site agents,
`AGENT_MAX_STEPS` caps an agent's turns, `AGENT_DUMP=<file>` writes the case file as JSON, and
`AGENT_TRACE=<folder>` saves each local agent turn (page, decision and result) for investigation.

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover tests
```

"""A conservative, no-model checklist for the tender portal's review page.

The clerk decides when it has reached a review page.  This module only reports
what the accessible page proves.  It tells two things apart:

- blockers: the page shows something wrong (an explicit error, an unfilled
  required control).  The final step is never pressed over these.
- unproven: the page does not show what a review must show (the tender
  reference, every offered position, the calculated total).  A click that
  "worked" proves nothing about what the portal holds, so the final step waits
  for a page that shows them; `submit.py` bounds that wait, because a signed
  bid scores and an unsigned one does not.

It never invents portal-specific field mappings.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal

from calculator import Bid

ERROR = re.compile(r"\b(error|invalid|failed|missing|fehler|ungültig|pflichtfeld)\b", re.I)
EMPTY_REQUIRED = re.compile(r"^(?=.*\(required\))(?=.*(?:value=\"\"|\[unchecked\])).*$", re.I)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Report:
    ready: bool
    blockers: tuple[str, ...]
    warnings: tuple[str, ...]
    checks: tuple[str, ...]
    unproven: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def text(self) -> str:
        state = "READY" if self.ready else "BLOCKED"
        lines = [f"PRE-SUBMISSION CHECKLIST: {state}", *[f"- {item}" for item in self.checks]]
        lines += [f"- BLOCKER: {item}" for item in self.blockers]
        lines += [f"- NOT SHOWN: {item}" for item in self.unproven]
        lines += [f"- WARNING: {item}" for item in self.warnings]
        if self.unproven:
            lines.append("This page does not show the whole bid. Open the form's review or summary step that lists "
                         "the reference, every position and the total, compare it with the bid sheet, correct what "
                         "differs, and check again there.")
        return "\n".join(lines)


def _money(value: Decimal) -> set[str]:
    fixed = f"{value:.2f}"
    whole, cents = fixed.split(".")
    return {fixed, fixed.replace(".", ","), f"{int(whole):,}.{cents}", f"{int(whole):,}".replace(",", ".") + "," + cents}


def check(page: str, bid: Bid, reference: str) -> Report:
    """Report review-page evidence without assuming a portal's labels or layout."""
    visible = re.sub(r"\[\d+\] ", "", page)
    lower = visible.lower()
    blockers: list[str] = []
    unproven: list[str] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []
    checks: list[str] = []
    errors = [line.strip() for line in visible.splitlines() if ERROR.search(line)]
    required = [line.strip() for line in visible.splitlines() if EMPTY_REQUIRED.match(line)]
    if errors:
        blockers.append("the portal reports: " + " | ".join(errors[:3])[:500])
    else:
        checks.append("no explicit portal error is visible")
    if required:
        blockers.append("a required control is empty or unchecked: " + " | ".join(required[:3])[:500])
    else:
        checks.append("no empty required control is visible")
    if reference and reference.lower() in lower:
        checks.append(f"tender reference {reference} is visible")
    else:
        unproven.append(f"tender reference {reference} is not visible on this page")
    expected = [line.position for line in bid.lines]
    missing = [position for position in expected if not re.search(rf"(?<![\w.-]){re.escape(position)}(?![\w.-])", visible)]
    if missing:
        unproven.append("offered position(s) not visible in this review: " + ", ".join(missing))
    else:
        checks.append("every offered position is visible")
    if bid.decision == "bid":
        if any(amount in visible for amount in _money(Decimal(bid.total_net))):
            checks.append("calculated total is visible")
        else:
            unproven.append(f"calculated total {Decimal(bid.total_net):.2f} is not visible on this page")
        # A unit price the page does not show is a hint for the clerk's own comparison, not proof of a mistake:
        # a review may list line totals only.
        unpriced = [line.position for line in bid.lines if line.position not in missing and line.unit_price is not None
                    and not any(amount in visible for amount in _money(Decimal(line.unit_price)))]
        if unpriced:
            warnings.append("unit price of the bid sheet not visible for position(s): " + ", ".join(unpriced))
        if bid.omitted:
            warnings.append("the calculator left out position(s): " + ", ".join(bid.omitted)
                            + "; they must not carry invented values")
    return Report(not blockers and not unproven, tuple(blockers), tuple(warnings), tuple(checks), tuple(unproven))

    """Strip contiguous blocks (>= 6 lines) from collected page i that already appeared in page i-1."""
    if len(pages) <= 1:
        return pages
    import difflib
    norm = lambda line: re.sub(r"\[\d+\]\s*", "", line).strip()
    out = [pages[0]]
    for prev, curr in zip(pages, pages[1:]):

"""Deterministic bid arithmetic for the RFQ-to-bid challenge.

The agents find and select the evidence; this module only applies the bid rules of the task brief to the structured
facts they filed: exact Decimal arithmetic, ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent, largest-remainder cent allocation, marginal
bonus bands, shared stock and delivery commitments. It contains no scenario values and never touches a website.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
from fractions import Fraction

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0")
HUNDRED = Decimal("100")

# Mass units to grams and index-rate units to EUR per gram, so any combination the sources use multiplies out.
MASS_TO_GRAMS = {"mg": Decimal("0.001"), "g": Decimal(1), "kg": Decimal(1000), "t": Decimal(1000000)}


def round_cents(value) -> Decimal:
    return Decimal(str(value)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def parse_number(raw, number_format: str | None = None) -> Decimal | None:
    """A number as written on a page ("1.234,56", "64,853 (en-US)", 12) as a Decimal; None when there is none.

    `number_format` is "de-DE" (decimal comma) or "en-US" (decimal point); an inline tag in `raw` wins. Without
    either, the separators decide, and a lone comma is read as a decimal comma, as German sources write it.
    """
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(raw, Decimal):
        return raw
    if isinstance(raw, (int, float)):
        return Decimal(str(raw))
    text = str(raw).strip()
    tag = re.search(r"(de-DE|en-US)", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    fmt = (tag.group(1) if tag else number_format or "").lower()
    match = re.search(r"[-+]?\d[\d.,'\s  ]*", text)
    if not match:
        return None
    token = re.sub(r"['\s  ]", "", match.group(0)).rstrip(".,")
    try:
        if fmt == "en-us":
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if fmt == "de-de":
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
        if "," in token and "." in token:
            if token.rfind(",") > token.rfind("."):
                return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if "," in token:
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ".")) if token.count(",") == 1 else Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if token.count(".") > 1:
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", ""))
        return Decimal(token)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def parse_when(raw, end_of_day: bool = False) -> datetime | None:
    """An ISO 8601 date or timestamp (as the extraction step writes them) as an aware UTC datetime.

    A value without a time is a whole day: its start, or its last microsecond with `end_of_day`, so that validity
    periods include both endpoints.
    """
    if not raw:
        return None
    text = str(raw).strip()
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text):
            day = datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return day + timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1) if end_of_day else day
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        german = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4})(?:[,\s]+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?", text)
        if not german:
            return None
        day, month, year, hour, minute = german.groups()
        try:
            when = datetime(int(year), int(month), int(day), int(hour or 0), int(minute or 0))
        except ValueError:
            return None
        if hour is None and end_of_day:
            when += timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1)
    return when.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if when.tzinfo is None else when.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def allocate_cents(total_cents: int, weights: dict[str, Decimal], method: str = "largest_remainder") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split `total_cents` across the keys in proportion to `weights`, as EUR amounts that sum exactly.

    Every share is floored to the cent; the cents left over go out by `method`: "largest_remainder" (ties to the
    lower key), "remainder_to_first", "remainder_to_last" or "remainder_to_largest" (the biggest weight).
    """
    keys = sorted(weights, key=position_order)
    total_weight = sum(weights.values(), ZERO)
    if not keys or total_cents <= 0 or total_weight <= 0:
        return {key: ZERO for key in keys}
    # Exact fractions: a tie between remainders must be a tie, not a matter of decimal precision.
    exact = {key: Fraction(total_cents) * Fraction(weights[key]) / Fraction(total_weight) for key in keys}
    cents = {key: math.floor(exact[key]) for key in keys}
    left = total_cents - sum(cents.values())
    if method == "remainder_to_first":
        cents[keys[0]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_last":
        cents[keys[-1]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_largest":
        cents[max(keys, key=lambda key: (weights[key], -keys.index(key)))] += left
    else:
        for key in sorted(keys, key=lambda key: (-(exact[key] - cents[key]), keys.index(key)))[:left]:
            cents[key] += 1
    return {key: Decimal(cents[key]) * CENT for key in keys}


def position_order(key) -> list:
    """Position identifiers in ascending order: their numbers count as numbers ("2" before "10")."""
    return [(0, int(part), "") if part.isdigit() else (1, 0, part) for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", str(key))]


def same_text(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Two attribute values name the same thing: case, spacing and punctuation aside."""
    def norm(value):
        return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zäöüß]+", "", (value or "").lower())
    return norm(a) == norm(b)


NO_CERTIFICATE = ("", "-", "keine", "kein", "ohne", "none", "no", "n/a", "na", "nicht gefordert", "keine gefordert",
                  "nicht erforderlich", "keine erforderlich", "entfällt")

    """Certifications match, with every way of writing "none required" counting as the same."""
    def norm(value):
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (value or "").strip().lower()).strip(" .—–")
        return "" if text in NO_CERTIFICATE else text
    return same_text(norm(a), norm(b))

# Goal: Improve the RFQ-to-Bid Agent Until It Achieves 100/100

You are responsible for iteratively improving and testing our Atira “RFQ to Bid” agent. Your goal is to achieve a **100/100 quality score while remaining eligible**. Treat eligibility as a hard requirement: a high score without a valid submitted answer does not meet the goal.

## Before changing anything

1. Read the repository’s `AGENTS.md`, `.entire/agent-guide.md`, and the Atira challenge rules and answer schema.
2. Review the current implementation, existing test results, run logs, and relevant project history. Follow the repository’s Entire workflow where required.

## Testing and improvement loop

Run **one test run at a time**. Do not start another until the current run has completed and been analyzed.

For each iteration:

1. State the specific hypothesis or issue being tested.

3. Run the test on the public scenario; do not make a scored submission.

6. Record what worked, what failed, what remains uncertain, and how the evidence supports those conclusions.
7. Compare the result with the previous baseline. Keep or revise the change based on evidence, not assumption.
8. Update a durable experiment log with the run ID, commit/package, hypothesis, changes, outcome, failure analysis, and next step.

- Respect the four-browser limit and all challenge rules.
- Generalize to the private dataset and unseen portal layouts; do not overfit to the public scenario.

## Success criteria

The goal is reached only when a completed test run is **eligible and scores 100/100**, with logs and page evidence showing the result was submitted and confirmed. If repeated runs do not reach 100, continue investigating and report the best verified score, remaining gaps, and the next evidence-based experiment. Do not claim that 100/100 is guaranteed.

# QuoteCraft — from RFQ to bid

A team of model-directed agents that reads a tender across four business websites it has never seen, works out the
bid the rules call for, and enters and signs it in the tender portal.

## How it works

```
task brief ──► model reads it: tender, scenario date, authorized senders
                    │
   ┌────────────────┼──────────────────┬─────────────────┐
   ▼                ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 agent            agent              agent             agent        one per website, each in its own browser:
 tender portal    supplier portal    ERP               webmail      the model picks every click, search and page
   │  keep          │  keep            │  keep           │  keep
   └────────────────┴───────┬──────────┴─────────────────┘
                            ▼
                     shared case file        a model call turns each filed page into typed facts;
                            │                the brief's rules yield the open questions all agents see
                            ▼
                      calculator.py          the bid rules as exact Decimal arithmetic
                            ▼
                     submission agent        fills the bid form it finds; the mail agent fetches the TAN
```

1. **Read the brief.** One model call extracts the tender reference, the scenario date, the bidder and which
   mailbox the rules authorize for which kind of record.
2. **Investigate in parallel.** One agent per website (`worker.Agent`). Each turn it sees its page as accessible
   text with numbered controls (`browser_env.Tab`), plus the case file and its open questions, and answers with
   actions: log in, click, fill, select, search, page through a list, download a file, or `keep` the page as
   evidence. After every browser action, a stable accessible-page fingerprint reports whether the page visibly
   changed, so silent portal failures become recovery hints rather than assumed success. Nothing in the code knows
   a URL, a selector or a click path of any website.
3. **File facts.** `keep` hands the page to a second model call that extracts typed records (positions, Q&A
   answers, revisions, requirements, materials, price conditions, mail records). `casefile.CaseFile` merges them
   and derives what is still unknown. A schema gate rejects malformed extraction envelopes and records before the
   merge. Each successful extraction retains its source URL, site agent, document ID,
   normalized result, and merge summary in the case-file dump, so later agents can assess contradictory evidence.
   A catalogue group found in the specification becomes an ERP question, a key
   in a Q&A answer becomes a mailbox question, and so on. Agents finish when their website has nothing left to add.
4. **Calculate.** `calculator.calculate_bid` applies the bid rules of the brief: latest clarification, withdrawn
   answers, scoped amendments, usable travel, sets to pieces, price scales, FX, conditional discount, condition
   clauses, shared stock, delivery commitments, cartons, pooled setup, project bonus, rounding. A position that
   lacks evidence is left out rather than guessed.
5. **Submit.** `submit.submit_bid` gives the bid to an agent on the tender portal, which fills whatever bid form
   it finds, asks a mail agent for the signing TAN, and runs a fresh live-page pre-submit report immediately before
   the irreversible confirmation. Explicit portal errors and empty required controls block that confirmation.

## What is model and what is code

| The model decides | Code does |
| --- | --- |
| where to go, what to search for, which record or document matters | renders the page, carries out the chosen action |
| how to pass a popup, access check, login or error page | retries a server error, re-reads the page |
| which page is evidence and of what kind | pages through a list the model chose, reads a file it chose |
| what a page says (extraction into typed facts) | parses numbers and dates, checks sender, reference and date |
| when a search is complete or a record does not exist | arithmetic, rounding, allocation |
| how to fill and sign the bid form | — |

No scenario value (reference, material, price, key, login, TAN) appears anywhere in the package.

## Files

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point: reads the run, starts the site agents, calculates, hands the bid to the submission agent |
| `worker.py` | The agent loop: page text in, the model's actions out |
| `browser_env.py` | A tab as accessible text (labels, descriptions, tooltips, frames, collapsed sections) and the actions on it |
| `casefile.py` | Evidence to typed facts with source provenance, open questions, calculator inputs |
| `calculator.py` | The bid rules as Decimal arithmetic |
| `submit.py` | Bid entry and signing |
| `preflight.py` | Non-model live review-page report that gates final confirmation on explicit errors or required inputs |
| `llm.py` | The hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy: JSON replies, retries, a concurrency cap |
| `run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py` | The starter kit's plumbing: the run contract, the run's browsers, the hosted models |
| `agent.json` | Setup (`uv sync`), run command, four browsers, the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The calculator rule by rule, the page rendering against local fixtures, the plumbing against fakes |

In the sandbox the platform sets everything (`CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`, `CDP_URLS`, `QWEN_*`):

atira test-run . --challenge rfq

def _int(value) -> int | None:
    """A whole number (quantity, stroke, carton size, weeks). "1.250" and "1,250" are one thousand two hundred and
    fifty here, not 1.25: a whole-number field has no decimals, so a separator before exactly three digits groups
    thousands, in German and in English writing alike."""
    if isinstance(value, str) and re.fullmatch(r"\s*\d{1,3}(?:[.,'  ]\d{3})+\s*", value):
        value = re.sub(r"[.,'  \s]", "", value)
    number = parse_number(value)
    return int(number) if number is not None else None


def _text(value) -> str | None:
    text = str(value).strip() if value is not None else ""
    return text if text and text.lower() not in ("null", "none", "n/a", "-", "—") else None


def _resolve_is_set(unit, flag) -> bool | None:
    text = (_text(unit) or "").lower()
    if text in _PIECE_UNITS:
        return False
    if text in _SET_UNITS:
        return True
    return flag if isinstance(flag, bool) else None


def _strip_physical_only_stock(text: str, data: dict | None) -> str:
    """Reject free_stock extracted from a plant-level physical summary that has not opened storage locations."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get("materials"), list):
        return ""
    lower = (text or "").lower()
    has_physical = any(term in lower for term in ("physischer bestand", "einschließlich prüfbestand", "physical stock"))
    has_free = any(term in lower for term in ("frei verwendbar", "verfügbarer gesamtbestand", "freier bestand",
                                              "frei verfügbar", "unrestricted", "free stock", "available stock"))
    if not has_physical or has_free:
        return ""
    stripped = False
    for row in data["materials"]:
        if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("free_stock") is not None:
            row.pop("free_stock", None)
            stripped = True
    return ("physical stock includes blocked/inspection stock — open the storage locations / availability "
            "breakdown to find and file freely available stock") if stripped else ""


def _dedup_collected_pages(pages: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Strip contiguous blocks (>= 6 lines) from collected page i that already appeared in page i-1."""
    if len(pages) <= 1:
        return pages
    import difflib
    norm = lambda line: re.sub(r"\[\d+\]\s*", "", line).strip()
    out = [pages[0]]
    for prev, curr in zip(pages, pages[1:]):
        prev_lines = prev.splitlines()
        curr_lines = curr.splitlines()
        prev_norm = [norm(line) for line in prev_lines]
        curr_norm = [norm(line) for line in curr_lines]
        drop: set[int] = set()
        for match in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, prev_norm, curr_norm, autojunk=False).get_matching_blocks():
            if match.size >= 6:
                for idx in range(max(8, match.b), match.b + match.size):
                    drop.add(idx)
        kept = [line for idx, line in enumerate(curr_lines) if idx not in drop]
        trimmed = "\n".join(kept).strip()
        out.append(trimmed if len(kept) >= 10 and len(trimmed) >= 40 else curr)
    return out


def _unit_is_set(unit) -> bool | None:
    """Classify only explicit, familiar piece/set unit labels; never guess from quantity or wording context."""
    value = _text(unit)
    if value is None:
        return None
    token = re.sub(r"[^a-zäöüß]", "", value.lower())
    if token in {"stk", "stück", "stueck", "pc", "pcs", "piece", "pieces", "unit", "units", "ea", "each"}:
        return False
    if token in {"satz", "sätze", "saetze", "set", "sets", "kit", "kits", "pack", "packs", "pair", "pairs", "garnitur", "garnituren"}:
        return True
    return None

"""Deterministic bid arithmetic for the RFQ-to-bid challenge.

The agents find and select the evidence; this module only applies the bid rules of the task brief to the structured
facts they filed: exact Decimal arithmetic, ROUND_HALF_UP to the cent, largest-remainder cent allocation, marginal
bonus bands, shared stock and delivery commitments. It contains no scenario values and never touches a website.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
from fractions import Fraction

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0")
HUNDRED = Decimal("100")

# Mass units to grams and index-rate units to EUR per gram, so any combination the sources use multiplies out.
MASS_TO_GRAMS = {"mg": Decimal("0.001"), "g": Decimal(1), "kg": Decimal(1000), "t": Decimal(1000000)}


def round_cents(value) -> Decimal:
    return Decimal(str(value)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def parse_number(raw, number_format: str | None = None) -> Decimal | None:
    """A number as written on a page ("1.234,56", "64,853 (en-US)", 12) as a Decimal; None when there is none.

    `number_format` is "de-DE" (decimal comma) or "en-US" (decimal point); an inline tag in `raw` wins. Without
    either, the separators decide, and a lone comma is read as a decimal comma, as German sources write it.
    """
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, bool):
        return None
    if isinstance(raw, Decimal):
        return raw
    if isinstance(raw, (int, float)):
        return Decimal(str(raw))
    text = str(raw).strip()
    tag = re.search(r"(de-DE|en-US)", text, re.IGNORECASE)
    fmt = (tag.group(1) if tag else number_format or "").lower()
    match = re.search(r"[-+]?\d[\d.,'\s  ]*", text)
    if not match:
        return None
    token = re.sub(r"['\s  ]", "", match.group(0)).rstrip(".,")
    try:
        if fmt == "en-us":
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if fmt == "de-de":
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
        if "," in token and "." in token:
            if token.rfind(",") > token.rfind("."):
                return Decimal(token.replace(".", "").replace(",", "."))
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if "," in token:
            return Decimal(token.replace(",", ".")) if token.count(",") == 1 else Decimal(token.replace(",", ""))
        if token.count(".") > 1:
            return Decimal(token.replace(".", ""))
        return Decimal(token)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def parse_when(raw, end_of_day: bool = False) -> datetime | None:
    """An ISO 8601 date or timestamp (as the extraction step writes them) as an aware UTC datetime.

    A value without a time is a whole day: its start, or its last microsecond with `end_of_day`, so that validity
    periods include both endpoints.
    """
    if not raw:
        return None
    text = str(raw).strip()
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text):
            day = datetime.fromisoformat(text).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return day + timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1) if end_of_day else day
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        german = re.search(r"(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\.(\d{4})(?:[,\s]+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?", text)
        if not german:
            return None
        day, month, year, hour, minute = german.groups()
        try:
            when = datetime(int(year), int(month), int(day), int(hour or 0), int(minute or 0))
        except ValueError:
            return None
        if hour is None and end_of_day:
            when += timedelta(days=1) - timedelta(microseconds=1)
    return when.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if when.tzinfo is None else when.astimezone(timezone.utc)


def allocate_cents(total_cents: int, weights: dict[str, Decimal], method: str = "largest_remainder") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split `total_cents` across the keys in proportion to `weights`, as EUR amounts that sum exactly.

    Every share is floored to the cent; the cents left over go out by `method`: "largest_remainder" (ties to the
    lower key), "remainder_to_first", "remainder_to_last" or "remainder_to_largest" (the biggest weight).
    """
    keys = sorted(weights, key=position_order)
    total_weight = sum(weights.values(), ZERO)
    if not keys or total_cents <= 0 or total_weight <= 0:
        return {key: ZERO for key in keys}
    # Exact fractions: a tie between remainders must be a tie, not a matter of decimal precision.
    exact = {key: Fraction(total_cents) * Fraction(weights[key]) / Fraction(total_weight) for key in keys}
    cents = {key: math.floor(exact[key]) for key in keys}
    left = total_cents - sum(cents.values())
    if method == "remainder_to_first":
        cents[keys[0]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_last":
        cents[keys[-1]] += left
    elif method == "remainder_to_largest":
        cents[max(keys, key=lambda key: (weights[key], -keys.index(key)))] += left
    else:
        for key in sorted(keys, key=lambda key: (-(exact[key] - cents[key]), keys.index(key)))[:left]:
            cents[key] += 1
    return {key: Decimal(cents[key]) * CENT for key in keys}


def position_order(key) -> list:
    """Position identifiers in ascending order: their numbers count as numbers ("2" before "10")."""
    return [(0, int(part), "") if part.isdigit() else (1, 0, part) for part in re.findall(r"\d+|\D+", str(key))]


def same_text(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Two attribute values name the same thing: case, spacing and punctuation aside."""
    def norm(value):
        return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zäöüß]+", "", (value or "").lower())
    return norm(a) == norm(b)


NO_CERTIFICATE = ("", "-", "keine", "kein", "ohne", "none", "no", "n/a", "na", "nicht gefordert", "keine gefordert",
                  "nicht erforderlich", "keine erforderlich", "entfällt")


def same_certification(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """Certifications match, with every way of writing "none required" counting as the same."""
    def norm(value):
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (value or "").strip().lower()).strip(" .—–")
        return "" if text in NO_CERTIFICATE else text
    return same_text(norm(a), norm(b))

class Material:
